item: A leaked liveness thread is stopped between tests; a boot-time pair refused for skew is counted and the last good pair is kept
summary: The CI flake seen once on #1375's test job: the oo-session-liveness daemon thread (record_boot -> start_liveness, stopped only by record_end) outlived its test and ticked the next test's vitals recorder on the real clock, so an injected 2023 tick read as a multi-year step back. tests/conftest.py _stop_leaked_liveness_thread() now stops it first in the autouse teardown (stop event and join; no stop_liveness(), which flushes). The coordinator's three lows on #1379: a tick with no usable boot-time pair no longer clears the forward-step baseline (_BOOT_BASE keeps the last good (wall, boot) pair, so a step of 600 s or more across such a tick is not lost); pairs refused for skew count in the persisted clock_boot_pairs_refused (a missing reading is not a refusal); a step is credited with opening a gap only when the baseline is the previous tick's own pair; the held-step test now fails when its guard goes; the _gaps docstring names the 1 s case. One independent read (0 block, 1 should-fix, 3 low) folded; 24 mutants killed; ruff advisory 417 of 417.
